A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Despite the title change and MCD-to-RaPA renaming, the shared algorithm and experiments clearly identify the same research work.

before.justification: V1 reports original targeted-attack experiments, defense evaluations, ablations and visualization results in Section 5 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: V2 retains original attack experiments and adds parameter-importance diagnostics, defense results and trained-surrogate comparisons in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The written mask distribution changes from Bernoulli(p) in v1 Equation (3) to Bernoulli(1-p) in v2 Equation (5), correcting the retention probability for the stated pruning rates. Otherwise, Algorithm 1 retains the same selected layers, gradient averaging and projected updates. The PDFs do not establish a changed implementation beyond this specification correction.

E1.justification: The ImageNet-compatible dataset, targeted classification task and CNN/Transformer/CLIP coverage remain. V2 adds evaluation under diffusion-based input purification through DiffPure in Section 4.4; no additional dataset or application domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds SIA throughout the main and appendix transfer comparisons, FTM to the RN50/DN121-to-Transformer comparison, and DSM and SASD-WS with their RaPA combinations in Table 7. These substantially expand evaluated comparators. DWP is discussed but has no reported comparison row.

E3.justification: The diagnostic design changes from perturbation masking to pruning the top/bottom 0.5% of parameters, measuring exponentially transformed importance with layerwise Gini coefficients, and sweeping importance-pruning rates. New trained-surrogate comparisons omit Weight Scaling for SASD-RaPA. The existing main attack budget, step size, batch size, iterations and inference count remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's perturbation-masking pilot and DropP/DropF experiments are removed. V2 adds importance-ranked pruning diagnostics, Gini analysis, a most-important-parameter masking sweep and training-framework compatibility analysis. Layer-selection, pruning-probability, compute-scaling and heatmap studies remain; the diversity/utility analysis moves to Appendix D.4.

E5.justification: V2 Tables 3–4 introduce ± values for RaPA where the corresponding v1 tables contain point estimates. Their statistical meaning, run counts and seeds are unspecified, so additional repeated runs cannot be established. The standard deviation across pruning-probability settings was already reported in v1.

E6.justification: Many new result entries accompany the added comparisons and diagnostics. Under retained main settings, reported RN50/DN121-to-Transformer averages change from 45.2/40.2 to 45.0/40.3. The strongest listed comparator changes from CFM at 32.2/22.3 to FTM at 33.3/22.8. Newly reported settings include 4.0% against DiffPure and 58.3% for DSM-RaPA; these are additions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Hessian-based parameter importance, its squared gradient-times-parameter approximation, and a second-order expected masked-loss derivation in Equations (3), (4), (7) and (8). Appendix B also formalizes the exponentially transformed importance metric and layerwise aggregation. V1 has no corresponding theoretical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace perturbation co-adaptation as the central diagnosis with over-reliance on a small parameter subset. V2 introduces the stronger claim that random pruning is equivalent to an importance-equalization regularizer and emphasizes training-free positioning. The broad transferability and compute-scaling claims remain.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanation shifts from dependent perturbation pixels/features to shortcut parameters and balanced parameter importance. V2 explains importance-pruning failure through degraded surrogate capacity and interprets trained-surrogate results as compatibility evidence. The diversity/utility tradeoff and limitation of weak CLIP-to-CNN transfer are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents the importance approximation, DepGraph parameter grouping, exponential transformation and Gini aggregation. Table 7 specifies omission of Weight Scaling in SASD-RaPA. V1's direct dataset-location link is replaced by a citation, while the core attack hyperparameters remain documented and unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning against FTM, DSM, SASD-WS and DWP, emphasizing training-free random pruning versus feature tuning, retraining and importance-based pruning. New OBD, importance-estimation and DepGraph references support the revised foundation. The original Dropout reference and its central motivational role are removed.

P1.justification: The title, method terminology, abstract, motivation and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background and related work are reorganized, detailed related work moves to Appendix A, compute scaling joins the ablation section, and diversity/utility moves to the appendix. New mathematical and ethical sections further restructure the document.

P2.justification: V2 removes v1's perturbation-masking Figures 2 and 8, adds pruning/Gini/compatibility tables, expands baseline rows and the defense table, and reformats main tables to accommodate ± values. Existing comparison tables are reordered and the diversity/utility figure moves to Appendix D with a corrected caption. Heatmaps and compute-scaling plots are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical assessment through newer comparators, parameter-pruning diagnostics and trained-surrogate combinations. However, its new central regularizer-equivalence claim is undermined by Appendix B.2: the stated mask gives E[Delta_i] = -p theta_i, so dropping that first-order term while retaining other order-p terms is unjustified; the derivation also confuses the second moment with variance. The added ± values remain undefined. These empirical benefits and substantive new theoretical problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
